flags.title: Dutch government think‑tank pushes EU for tougher tariffs and controls on China
flags.summary: "If we do not find a solution for the distorted trade, we risk spending a lot of money while losing European gains in areas such as privacy, working conditions and climate," warned Corien Prins, chair of the Dutch science council.

flags.title: First fully-autonomous drone kill Ukraine heralds ‘dystopian future of untethered weaponry’
flags.summary: For the first time ever, a target was selected not by a human, but by artificial intelligence.

flags.title: EU budget must bankroll Europe’s independence, von der Leyen says
flags.summary: Commission president’s pitch for a €2 trillion spending plan comes as the bloc weighs how to reduce its reliance on the U.S. and China — and faces a German-led push for hundreds of billions of euros in cuts.

flags.title: After today’s Independence Day parade, Moldova needs hard security guarantees against Moscow
flags.summary: On Thursday (27 August), Moldova marks 35 years of independence, and for the first time in its history, the day will be marked with a military parade through Chișinău.That single fact says more about European security than any communiqué.

flags.title: Poland asks EU to fine Meta €250 million over scam ads
flags.summary: Polish authorities have notified Meta multiple times, but the company still hasn't offered "an effective and adequate response" to the issue, the country's deputy prime minister writes.

flags.title: Turkey is defying Europe’s human-rights court — and Osman Kavala is paying the price
flags.summary: More than 10 years after the failed coup attempt and more than 13 years since the Gezi Park protests, the distance that Turkey has travelled along the authoritarian path is starkly clear. This direction is reversible. But the Turkish authorities have made clear that they do not intend to shift their path, warn Amnesty International.

flags.summary: Ukraine already faces a €23 billion hole in its defense budget.

flags.title: Lobbyists grumble over soaring conference prices — then pay up to court Britain’s new power players
flags.summary: The cost of attending the ruling Labour Party's business day has gone up 83 percent in two years.
